1: Chapter 1: The Guest on a Rainy Night
Rain had been falling on Doldari for three days. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village's small pharmacy alone.
As evening fell, she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when a frantic knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"

At the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin. Blood had seeped through the cloth wrapped around his left arm. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was a member of the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat my wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay you. Would three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oiled paper from his robe. "This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by May 18."
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors had already been jealous that the pharmacy was doing well, and now a stranger had come knocking in the middle of the night.
Even so, Haneul refused the money and said only, "I'll guide you to the mountain early tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they met an old man, Lee Youngsoo, who was chopping firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. He said that the night before, three strangers had been looking for a wounded young man at the edge of the village.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each step firmly, one step at a time. Park Junho followed silently behind.

By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist was slowly lifting, and in the distance the roof of Cheongpungsa came into view. A nun stood at the temple gate. She was Jeonghye, the nun who received guests at the temple.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul smiled and replied, "Then next time you come, you can fix the roof of the apothecary." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
